name: Productize a freelance service: fixed scope/price/timeline plus sustainable operating constraints
goal: Turn repeatable freelance work into a productized offer (predetermined deliverable, fixed price, fixed timeline, inclusions/exclusions, ideal-client qualification) that lets buyers skip custom scoping, then harden it with operating constraints—capacity caps, revision limits, allowed stack, rush fees—and a standard intake→produce→QA→handoff checklist so delivery stays sustainable.

sources.title: You Should Productize Your Service - Here Is How To Do It!
how to actually build a sustainable productized service ($20k+)

prerequisites: A service you have delivered multiple times

inputs.name: target_client
inputs.description: Ideal buyer (e.g. startup-like buyers wanting a known outcome fast)

inputs.name: draft_offer
inputs.description: Existing package to harden, if any

outputs.name: productized_offer
outputs.description: Named package with scope/price/timeline/exclusions and explicit ops constraints

constraints: Operational freelancing/product procedure only — no get-rich-quick claims.
Ground every step in YouTube-provided captions; adapt UI labels if the product renamed menus.
Only package repeatable work; exclude open-ended R&D.

steps.action: Define the offer as prepackaged: predetermined cost + predetermined scope + stated result in a stated timebox.
Name the sales benefit: productizing skips mutual scoping foreplay when the client wants a known outcome fast (startup-like buyers).
Write inclusions vs exclusions to escape unique-every-time projects that burn you out and cede control to clients.
Publish a fixed price and turnaround so buyers can skip long rate/scope negotiation.
State ideal client and when NOT to buy (heavy custom → separate bespoke engagement). Acknowledge why large heterogeneous agencies often avoid pure SKUs; choose the repeatable-SKU lane deliberately.
Add constraints: capacity caps, revision limits, allowed tech stack, rush fees — small tweaks that preserve happiness on both sides.
Standardize intake → produce → QA → handoff checklist/templates for every order.
Align internal fulfillment with client expectation so the package is sustainable, not only marketable.
